items.item: All drawings develop the masterplan and analysis into compatible section geometry, facility boundaries, paving, planting and lighting.
Both ground sheets repeat the analysis's four correct zone names and areas; planting names and quantities agree with the fixed records.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The plan and entrance views establish exposed concrete structure, distinct sports bays, passage on the south and seating integrated with planting on the north. Visible wayfinding assigns Shared Way to the through-route and Activity Floor to the sports area. Perspective occlusion is allowed; reversed zoning, concealed or replaced concrete structure, misplaced labels or seating that blocks the route fails.

Read the schedules, dimensions and relevant details against the records: Shared Way and approaches use broom-finished concrete; Service Strip uses brushed concrete and flush steel grating; basketball uses acrylic-coated asphalt; tennis and fitness use wet-pour rubber over concrete. Planters are freestanding precast concrete, 600 mm high, with 450 mm growing medium and internal drip irrigation; seats use timber slats on freestanding steel frames. Basketball mesh is freestanding and 3,000 mm high, and other new fixtures are freestanding and no higher than 3,000 mm above local ground. The transverse drawing retains 1,200 mm square column shafts and centred 2,400 mm foundations; bridge coverage begins at y = 6,000 mm and its underside is z = 6,240 mm above the southwest datum. Relevant information may be distributed across these sheets; contradictory assemblies, structural attachments or dimensions fail.

Read any operating annotations as records: access is daily 06:00–22:00, sports are daily 08:00–21:00, and passage lighting operates from dusk until 22:00. Depicted use must agree: the 10:00 scene permits active sport and crossing, while 21:30 retains lit public passage and inactive sports equipment. These image roles need not print an hours table, but conflicting stated hours, a closed night through-route or active night sport fails.

The analysis establishes an upstream zoning record with the four correct name–area pairs, totalling 1,728 m², and the presentation repeats them. Check available process or submission sequencing for the analysis preceding applications; filenames alone do not establish chronology. Incorrect source facts or missing presentation repetitions fail; image repetitions are additionally checked through carry-through and the drawing set.

The single-page analysis records the four zones with their specified areas and surfaces, open sky over Shared Way and Service Strip, bridge shade over Activity Floor from y = 6 m and over Garden Edge, and allowances of 40 moving users, 2 maintenance staff, 40 sports users and spectators, and 18 seated users respectively. Identify the three specified botanical species. Table or prose layout is acceptable; missing fields, swapped allowances or substituted species fail.

The plan establishes the full boundary, southern 4 m clear connection, six centred 4 m protection squares at x = 12, 36, 60 m and y = 8, 20 m, and full-length drainage at y = 4.5–4.8 m. Dimensioned sections cut x = 36 m transversely and y = 2 m longitudinally, retaining geometry appropriate to each cut. The transverse section labels northward 1% ground rise, minimum 6,000 mm bridge clearance and maximum 3,000 mm fixtures and shows drainage and intersected foundations. Off-cut objects may be referenced or projected instead of falsely intersected. Wrong cuts, obstructed route, altered protected footprints or missing required labels fail.

Place B1 at x = 16–32 m, y = 7.5–19.5 m; T1 at x = 40–46 m and T2 at x = 46–52 m, both y = 8–18 m; and F1 at x = 64–70 m, y = 8–18 m. Show one hoop, one table per tennis envelope, one pull-up station and two stretching rails, with seating and approaches around the envelopes. Dimension the basketball edge and route/service interface on the primary sheet, the tennis spectator edge on its sheet, and the fitness footing and approach on its sheet. Local details must be traceable to the plan and use scheduled materials. Alternate drawing conventions are allowed; moved or merged envelopes, missing equipment or interfaces, undimensioned details and material conflicts fail.

Masterplan and planting layout identify the site and the analysis's three botanical species. Both ground sheets repeat all four zone name–area pairs. The planting layout keys DF, CP and GM to totals 72, 96 and 120, with 12, 16 and 20 respectively in each of six 6 m × 2 m beds. Beds occupy y = 22–24 m and x = 4–10, 16–22, 28–34, 40–46, 52–58 and 64–70 m. The second ground sheet resolves surface junctions and locates lighting consistently with the plan. Keyed schedules are allowed; wrong planting locations, quantities, names or conflicting light locations fail. Presentation text is checked through carry-through and content.

All three stills depict the planned facilities, beds, columns and lights from the named entrances. The east day/night pair preserves camera position, direction and framing; people and illumination may change. At 10:00 show active sports and everyday passage; at 21:30 show lit passage and resting sports equipment. Occlusion is acceptable; scene redesign, a changed paired camera or contradictory use fails.

Review the whole film and its playback duration. It lasts 12 seconds and progresses from an occupied sports boundary with spectators during the 18:30 sports session to lit Shared Way passage at 21:30, when sports equipment is inactive. Facilities, planting and lighting retain plan locations throughout. Camera movement and editing are flexible; wrong duration, omitted temporal state, absent spectators, active late sports or a changing layout fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has eight or more pages and legibly states daily public access of 06:00–22:00 and sports use of 08:00–21:00. It repeats NORTH SPAN, the four correct zone names and areas, and all three botanical names from the analysis. Page composition is flexible; too few pages, missing required facts or inconsistent operating hours fails.

Every listed source is visibly reused and recognizable in the presentation. Scaling, cropping and page recomposition are acceptable when identifying drawing or image content remains readable. A title-only reference, substitute design, illegible thumbnail or omitted source fails.

Provide a readable north arrow, scale bar, boundary dimensions, sports-envelope outlines, protection squares and lighting symbols. Repeat the analysis's four zone name–area pairs and three botanical names. The four full-width bands use y boundaries 0, 4, 5.5, 21 and 24 m. Different legible notation is allowed; omitted annotations, inconsistent source facts or shifted band boundaries fail.

All drawings develop the masterplan and analysis into compatible section geometry, facility boundaries, paving, planting and lighting. Both ground sheets repeat the analysis's four correct zone names and areas; planting names and quantities agree with the fixed records.

All entrance perspectives depict the same planned space, and the east day/night pair retains its camera and framing. The day scene supports active sport and crossing, while night scenes preserve illuminated passage with inactive sports equipment.

carryThrough.notes: The three site specification records precede the applications; the analysis, masterplan, four ground and planting sheets and presentation repeat Shared Way at 288 m², Service Strip at 108 m², Activity Floor at 1,116 m² and Garden Edge at 216 m².

The masterplan, paving and planting layout and presentation print NORTH SPAN and all three botanical names from the analysis schedule; the paving and planting layout identifies DF × 72, CP × 96 and GM × 120 within six 6 m × 2 m beds and repeats all four zone names.
